quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit.
You can complete the pass in a no passing zone if you started before the zone began.
You may exceed the speed limit.
Pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit.
questions.explanation: All passes must follow the speed limit and only happen where passing is allowed.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: A proper lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you set up for turns.
Give you an escape route.
Help you avoid wind blasts from other vehicles.
Put you in another vehicle's blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put you in another vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and lets them see you. It helps you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and hazards. It also discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if needed.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle properly, how should you sit?

options.text: Use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up.
Sit far back on the seat so your arms stay straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Drag your feet on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can control the motorcycle with your arms, not use them to hold yourself up. Your arms should bend slightly at the handlebars. Keep your knees against the gas tank and your feet on the footrests to stay balanced.

questions.question: What is true about a windshield?

options.text: It is a good substitute for a face shield.
It does not fully protect your eyes from the wind.
It is required on all motorcycles.
You should use one on windy days.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not fully protect your eyes from the wind.
questions.explanation: A windshield cannot replace goggles or a face shield. Most windshields do not protect your eyes from wind.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Roll on the throttle.
Hold the handlebars loosely.
Gently apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
Speed up to get off the road faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, ease off the throttle and go straight as you slow down. If you must brake, gently apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.

questions.question: When being passed, which of the following is NOT a hazard?

options.text: Extended mirrors.
Objects being thrown from other vehicles.
Wind blasts.
Headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Headlights.
questions.explanation: When being passed, watch out for the passing vehicle's mirrors. Be aware of wind gusts and objects that might be thrown by passengers. Headlights are not a hazard when being passed.

questions.question: Where is the rear brake control usually located?

options.text: On the right handlebar.
On the left handlebar.
Near the left foot.
Near the right foot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right foot.
questions.explanation: The rear brake is operated with the right foot.

questions.question: What is often found in the center of the lane?

options.text: A landing strip
An oily or greasy strip
Lane markings
Ice

questions.correctAnswerText: An oily or greasy strip
questions.explanation: Oil drippings from cars form an oily strip in the center of each lane. It is usually still safe for a motorcycle to ride on this strip unless the road is wet.

questions.question: When braking, what should you do?

options.text: Use only one brake in non-emergency situations.
Use both brakes only when riding on wet pavement.
Use both brakes every time.
Use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes every time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What happens when your rear tire skids?

options.text: It is not serious.
You lose the ability to change direction.
It will fix itself.
It only matters if the front tire is also skidding.

questions.correctAnswerText: You lose the ability to change direction.
questions.explanation: A skidding rear tire is dangerous and can cause a serious crash or injury. When the rear wheel locks up, you cannot change direction. Release the brake to regain control.

questions.question: What happens if you shift to a lower gear while going too fast?

options.text: Your motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid.
The horn may go off.
Your motorcycle may jerk and the front tire may skid.
Your motorcycle may jerk and a warning light may turn on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear while going too fast can cause your motorcycle to jerk and the rear tire to skid. This makes you lose control. Always slow down before shifting to a lower gear.

questions.question: Which statement about motorcycle brakes is true?

options.text: The front and rear brakes have equal stopping power.
The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
The rear brake is more powerful than the front brake.
Only the front brake should be used when stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake provides most of the stopping power—at least 70 percent. Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Where is the engine cut-off switch located?

options.text: Near the left handgrip
Near the right handgrip
Near the left footrest
Near the right footrest

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right handgrip
questions.explanation: The engine cut-off switch is located next to the right handgrip. Know where all your motorcycle's controls are before you start riding.

questions.question: What should rain suits do?

options.text: Should not be used.
Should not puff up when riding.
Are not needed because motorcycles should not be ridden in rain.
Should tear easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not puff up when riding.
questions.explanation: Good rain suits made for motorcycle riding will not tear or puff up when you ride at high speeds.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what should you NOT tell them to do?

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after you start the engine.
Sit as far forward as they can without crowding you.
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.
Talk whenever they want.

questions.correctAnswerText: Talk whenever they want.
questions.explanation: Passengers should not talk or move around unnecessarily so you can focus on riding. Passengers should get on only after the engine starts. They should sit forward without crowding you and hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Move your position in the lane as needed and adjust to conditions.
Ride faster than usual to reach your destination quickly.
Always use your low beam headlight to see better.
Follow closely behind other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your position in the lane as needed and adjust to conditions.
questions.explanation: Be ready to change your lane position, especially at night. Use safe riding practices when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: What should you do if you must ride over an obstacle?

options.text: Slow down as much as possible.
Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Speed up if you can.
Stay in your seat and lift your feet off the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as much as possible.
questions.explanation: Slow down before hitting an obstacle. Approach it at a 90-degree angle if possible. Keep your motorcycle straight up. Just before you hit it, ease off the throttle to lighten the front end.

questions.question: What can happen if you shift to a lower gear while going too fast?

options.text: Your motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid.
Your motorcycle may speed up too quickly.
The front tire will likely skid.
The engine will make a loud noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear while going too fast will cause your motorcycle to jerk and the rear wheel may skid.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift lever located?

options.text: In front of the left footrest
In front of the right footrest
On the left handgrip
On the right handgrip

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is located in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.
